answer: Sybil resistance via verifiable-delay admission. To register, an agent must compute a verifiable delay function: a strictly sequential computation taking about ten minutes however many cores it rents, quartz-clock-stamped by peers to prevent precomputation. The proof is deposited into a per-identity vault locking the newcomer's first epoch of earnings. Since the delay is sequential, minting N fake agents costs N full delays, zero parallel discount, while an honest applicant pays once. Validators drawn into shifting nebula cohorts attest which identities produced proofs on schedule.
